name: Mandative should
pattern: content clause[(that) + Subject + should + plain-form VP]

entry.name: Mandative should
entry.pattern: content clause[(that) + Subject + should + plain-form VP]

1.definition: Realizes a requirement or recommendation with a specialized modal.

examples.form: It is essential [that the gate should remain closed].

projection.target: Should is possible with strongly requiring predicates such as essential. This modal need not weaken the strength of the matrix requirement.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Should after a strong requirement
curious.summary: After a word that states a strong requirement, a that-clause can use should to say what is required.
curious.body: In It is essential that the gate should remain closed, the should is part of the requirement. The clause after that tells us what has to happen to the gate. A word like essential strongly requires something, and should can follow it in this way. The should doesn't weaken the requirement. It doesn't turn the sentence into a mild piece of advice. This dictionary also has a related entry for a version without should, which can replace it in the same kind of sentence.

examples.text: It is essential [that the gate should remain closed].

curious.try: Say It is essential that the gate should remain closed. Is the requirement strong or weak?

teacher.summary: Helps explain should in that-clauses after strongly requiring words like essential, and why it doesn't soften the requirement.
teacher.explain: In a mandative content clause, should can follow the subject and take a plain-form VP: that the gate should remain closed. The pattern realizes a requirement or recommendation. Should is possible with strongly requiring predicates such as essential, and the modal need not weaken the strength of the matrix requirement. This dictionary has a separate entry for the alternating form without should. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional and short.
teacher.terms: Mandative construction is the usual name. The related form without should is called the subjunctive mandative in this dictionary.

examples.text: It is essential [that the gate should remain closed].

contrasts.text: It is essential that the gate should remain closed.
contrasts.note: Strongly requiring predicate with should; the requirement isn't weakened.

watch_for: A learner might hear should as mild advice, when here it need not weaken the strength of the requirement.
A learner might read should as a prediction about the gate, when it states what is required.
teacher.activity: Students complete sentences beginning It is essential that ... with a subject and should plus a plain verb, then discuss how strong each requirement feels.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Mandative should." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/mandative-should-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
